title: 2026 UK ETS CCS onshore-regulator consultation QA controls

sources.title: UK Emissions Trading Scheme: Regulating cross-boundary CCS pipelines
UK ETS: Regulating cross-boundary CCS pipelines (accessible webpage)

facts.source_fact: The Authority consulted on whether one UK ETS permit could cover the onshore portion of a cross-boundary CCS pipeline.
facts.expected_handling: Label as consultation option, not commenced rule.

facts.source_fact: Option 1 would assign a single onshore regulator.
facts.expected_handling: Preserve option number and proposal status.

facts.source_fact: Potential Option 1 criteria include central control room location.
facts.expected_handling: Do not treat criterion as adopted.

facts.source_fact: Potential Option 1 criteria include the operator's UK-registered office location.
Potential Option 1 criteria include the jurisdiction containing most pipeline length.
The consultation proposes Authority designation if regulator assignment remains uncertain.
Option 2 would jointly confer functions on relevant regulators and identify a lead regulator.
If regulators could not reach consensus under Option 2, the Authority could designate an appropriate regulator under the proposal.
facts.expected_handling: Do not present as current exercised power.

facts.source_fact: The operator would be told by regulators how it would be regulated and how to apply for a permit under the proposed arrangements.
Consultation responses are intended to inform later final policy decisions.
facts.expected_handling: Do not infer implementation from consultation closure.
